tools.name: Word Counter
tools.summary: Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs as you type, with reading time, speaking time and your most-used keywords.
steps: Type or paste your text into the box.
Watch the counts update instantly as you write.
Check the keyword list to spot words you repeat too often.
tools.about: Whether you are writing an essay with a word limit, a blog post that should be long enough to rank, or a script that has to fit a two-minute video, knowing your exact length saves time. Reading time assumes about 230 words per minute and speaking time about 140, which are typical averages for adults.

faqs.q: How are words counted?
faqs.a: Any group of letters or numbers separated by spaces or punctuation counts as one word. Hyphenated words like “well-known” count as one.

faqs.q: Is my text saved anywhere?
faqs.a: No. Everything is counted inside your browser. Your text is never sent to a server.

faqs.q: How long should a blog post be?
faqs.a: There is no fixed rule, but posts that fully answer a question are usually 800–2,000 words. Write until the topic is covered, then stop.

tools.name: Character Counter
tools.summary: Count characters with and without spaces, and see instantly whether your text fits limits for X (Twitter), Instagram, SMS, meta descriptions and more.
steps: Paste or type your text.
See the total characters, with and without spaces.
Check the platform bars to see how much room you have left on each.
tools.about: Most platforms cut off text that runs too long: a post on X allows 280 characters, an Instagram caption 2,200, a single SMS 160, and Google usually shows around 155–160 characters of a meta description. This counter shows all of these at once so you can write to fit before you publish.

faqs.q: Do spaces count as characters?
faqs.a: On almost every platform, yes. That’s why the main number includes spaces. The “without spaces” figure is useful for some school and translation work.

faqs.q: Do emojis count as one character?
faqs.a: This counter counts each emoji as one character, the way you see it. Some platforms, like X, count most emojis as two, so leave a little room there.

faqs.q: Why does my SMS split into two messages?
faqs.a: A standard SMS holds 160 characters. Longer messages are split, and using emojis or some special characters lowers the limit to 70.

tools.name: Case Converter
tools.summary: Change text to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case and more in one click, then copy the result.
steps: Paste your text into the box.
Click the case you want — the text changes immediately.
Press Copy to use it anywhere.
tools.about: Fix text that was typed with Caps Lock on, turn a sentence into a proper headline, or prepare variable names for code. Title Case keeps small words like “and”, “of” and “the” in lowercase unless they start the title, which is how most style guides write headlines.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Title Case and Capitalized Case?
faqs.a: Capitalized Case makes the first letter of every word uppercase. Title Case leaves short words such as “a”, “in” and “of” lowercase, which reads more naturally in headlines.

faqs.q: Can I undo a change?
faqs.a: Yes — press Undo to return to your previous text.

faqs.q: Does it work with other languages?
faqs.a: Upper and lower case work for any language that has them, such as English, French or Turkish. Languages without cases, like Urdu or Arabic, are left as they are.

tools.name: Age Calculator
tools.summary: Find your exact age in years, months and days, the total days you have lived, and how long until your next birthday.
steps: Choose your date of birth.
Leave “age on” as today, or pick another date to check age on that day.
Read your exact age, totals and the countdown to your next birthday.
tools.about: Exact age is needed for job applications, exams, visas and admissions that set minimum or maximum ages on a certain date. This calculator counts full calendar months and days, so it handles leap years and months of different lengths correctly.

faqs.q: How is age calculated?
faqs.a: It counts complete years first, then complete months, then the remaining days between the two dates.

faqs.q: What if I was born on 29 February?
faqs.a: In years without a 29 February, your birthday is treated as 1 March for the countdown.

faqs.q: Can I calculate age on a future date?
faqs.a: Yes. Change the “age on” date to any date, for example the closing date of an application.

tools.name: Percentage Calculator
tools.summary: Work out X% of a number, what percent one number is of another, and the percentage increase or decrease between two values.
steps: Pick the type of question you have.
Enter the two numbers.
Read the answer and the formula used to get it.
tools.about: Percentages come up everywhere: discounts, exam marks, salary raises, tax and growth figures. The three calculators here cover the questions people ask most, and each one shows the working so you can check it or use it again later.

faqs.q: How do I calculate a percentage of a number?
faqs.a: Multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100. For example, 15% of 2,000 is 2,000 × 15 ÷ 100 = 300.

faqs.q: How is percentage change calculated?
faqs.a: Subtract the old value from the new value, divide by the old value, then multiply by 100. A positive result is an increase; a negative result is a decrease.

faqs.q: Why is a 50% drop not undone by a 50% rise?
faqs.a: Because each percentage is taken from a different starting value. 100 down 50% is 50; 50 up 50% is only 75.

tools.name: BMI Calculator
tools.summary: Calculate your Body Mass Index in metric or imperial units and see which standard BMI range it falls into.
steps: Choose metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb, ft/in).
Enter your weight and height.
See your BMI, its range, and the healthy weight range for your height.
tools.about: BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. The World Health Organization groups adult BMI as underweight (below 18.5), healthy (18.5–24.9), overweight (25–29.9) and obese (30 or more). It is a quick screening number only — it does not measure body fat directly and does not suit children, pregnant women or very muscular people. For advice about your health, talk to a doctor.

faqs.q: Is BMI accurate?
faqs.a: It is a useful rough guide for most adults, but it cannot tell muscle from fat, so athletes may show a high BMI while being healthy.

faqs.q: Can children use this calculator?
faqs.a: No. Children and teenagers are measured with age- and sex-specific BMI charts, which this calculator does not use.

faqs.q: Are the ranges the same for everyone?
faqs.a: These are the WHO ranges for adults. Some health bodies suggest lower cut-offs for people of South Asian descent, so ask a doctor what applies to you.

tools.name: Unit Converter
tools.summary: Convert length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed and data size between metric and imperial units instantly.
steps: Choose what you are converting, like length or weight.
Type a value and pick the “from” unit.
See it converted to every other unit at once.
tools.about: Convert between kilometres and miles, kilograms and pounds, Celsius and Fahrenheit, square feet and marla, litres and gallons, and more. Data sizes are shown in both decimal (1 MB = 1,000 KB) and the binary units computers often use (1 MiB = 1,024 KiB).

faqs.q: How big is a marla?
faqs.a: Marla sizes differ by area. This converter uses 1 marla = 272.25 sq ft (the traditional standard). Some housing societies use 225 or 250 sq ft, so check the size your seller is using.

faqs.q: Why are there two kinds of gallons?
faqs.a: A US gallon is about 3.785 litres and an imperial (UK) gallon is about 4.546 litres. Both are listed.

faqs.q: Why does my 1 TB drive show less space?
faqs.a: Drive makers use decimal units (1 TB = 1,000 GB), while many computers show binary units (1 TiB = 1,024 GiB), so 1 TB appears as about 931 GiB.

tools.name: Time Zone Converter
tools.summary: Convert a time between any time zones — like Pakistan, New York, London and Dubai — with daylight saving handled automatically.
steps: Set the date and time, and the time zone it is in.
Add the cities or zones you want to compare.
See the matching local time everywhere, including the day.
tools.about: Planning a call with a client in the US or a meeting across offices is easy to get wrong, especially when daylight saving time starts or ends. This converter uses your browser’s built-in time zone database, so summer and winter time changes are applied for the date you choose.

faqs.q: Does it handle daylight saving time?
faqs.a: Yes. The offset is worked out for the exact date you enter, so times stay correct when clocks change.

faqs.q: What time zone is Pakistan in?
faqs.a: Pakistan Standard Time is UTC+5 all year. It does not currently use daylight saving time.

faqs.q: Why do US times shift by an hour during the year?
faqs.a: Most of the US moves its clocks forward in spring and back in autumn, so the gap with Pakistan changes between, for example, 9 and 10 hours for New York.

tools.name: Profit Margin Calculator
tools.summary: Calculate profit, margin and markup from cost and selling price — or find the selling price you need for a target margin.
steps: Choose whether you know the selling price or a target margin.
Enter your cost and price (or margin).
Read the profit, margin and markup.
tools.about: Margin and markup are often confused. Margin is profit as a share of the selling price; markup is profit as a share of the cost. Buying at 800 and selling at 1,000 gives a 20% margin but a 25% markup. Pricing with the right one protects your profit.

faqs.q: What is a good profit margin?
faqs.a: It depends on the industry. Retail and mobile phone sales often run on thin margins, while services and digital products can have much higher ones.

faqs.q: How do I price for a 30% margin?
faqs.a: Divide your cost by (1 − 0.30). A cost of 700 needs a price of 1,000 for a 30% margin. Use the “target margin” mode to do this instantly.

faqs.q: Should I include delivery and fees in cost?
faqs.a: Yes. Include every cost of making one sale — product, delivery, payment fees and packaging — to see your true margin.

tools.name: Loan / EMI Calculator
tools.summary: Calculate the monthly installment (EMI) for a car, home or personal loan, with total interest and a month-by-month repayment schedule.
steps: Enter the loan amount, yearly interest rate and loan period.
See your monthly installment, total interest and total payment.
Open the schedule to see how each payment splits between interest and principal.
tools.about: EMI stands for Equated Monthly Installment — the same payment every month until the loan is paid off. Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal. Banks may add processing fees, insurance or taxes, so treat this as an estimate and confirm the final figures with your lender.

faqs.q: How is EMI calculated?
faqs.a: EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate and n is the number of months.

faqs.q: Does this work for Islamic financing?
faqs.a: Islamic car and home financing uses rental or profit rates instead of interest, but the monthly figure is often worked out the same way. Ask your bank for its exact method.

faqs.q: How can I lower my EMI?
faqs.a: A larger down payment, a lower rate or a longer period all reduce the EMI — though a longer period usually means paying more in total.

tools.name: Discount & Sales Tax Calculator
tools.summary: Find the sale price after a discount, add sales tax (GST) to a price, or remove tax from a tax-inclusive price.
steps: Pick discount, add tax or remove tax.
Enter the price and the percentage.
See the final price and exactly how much you save or pay in tax.
tools.about: Check what a “40% off” deal really costs, work out the price including GST before sending a quote, or find out how much tax is hidden in a price that already includes it. The tax rate starts at 18%, Pakistan’s standard sales tax rate at the time of writing — change it to whatever rate applies to you.

faqs.q: How do I remove tax from a price?
faqs.a: Divide the price by 1 plus the tax rate. A price of 1,180 with 18% tax included is 1,180 ÷ 1.18 = 1,000 before tax.

faqs.q: Are two discounts the same as adding them up?
faqs.a: No. 20% off and then another 10% off is 28% off in total, not 30%, because the second discount applies to the already-reduced price.

faqs.q: Is the tax rate always 18%?
faqs.a: No — rates differ by country, province, product and service, and they change over time. Always enter the rate that applies to your sale.

tools.name: Invoice Generator
tools.summary: Create a clean, professional invoice in minutes — add your items, tax and discount, then download it as a PDF. Free, no sign-up.

tools.about: A clear invoice gets you paid faster. Add your business name, payment details and due date, and the totals are calculated for you. Your details are remembered in this browser for next time, but nothing is uploaded — the PDF is created on your own device.

faqs.q: Is this invoice legally valid?
faqs.a: An invoice is a record of a sale. If you are registered for sales tax, your country may require extra details such as your tax number — add them in the notes field.

faqs.q: Are my invoices saved?
faqs.a: Your own business details are remembered in this browser to save typing. Download each invoice as a PDF to keep a copy.

faqs.q: Can I use a different currency?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose PKR, USD, GBP, EUR, AED or SAR, or type any currency symbol.

tools.name: Image Compressor
tools.summary: Reduce JPG, PNG and WebP image file sizes in your browser. Compress several images at once and download them individually or as a ZIP.
steps: Drop your images in, or click to choose them.
Adjust quality and the maximum width if you want smaller files.
Download each image, or all of them together as a ZIP.
tools.about: Smaller images make websites load faster, emails send quicker and uploads meet size limits. A quality of around 70–80% usually cuts file size by more than half with no visible difference. Your images never leave your device — they are compressed right here in the browser.

faqs.q: Are my images uploaded?
faqs.a: No. Compression happens entirely in your browser, so your photos stay private.

faqs.q: Which format should I choose?
faqs.a: JPG or WebP for photos, PNG for graphics with sharp edges or transparency. WebP is usually the smallest.

faqs.q: Why did a PNG get bigger?
faqs.a: PNG is lossless, so some already-optimised PNGs can’t shrink further. Try saving as WebP or JPG instead.

tools.name: Image Resizer
tools.summary: Resize images to exact pixel dimensions or by percentage, with presets for Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and passport-size photos.
steps: Add one or more images.
Enter a width and height, a percentage, or pick a preset.
Download the resized images.
tools.about: Social platforms, job portals and online forms often ask for images at a specific size. Keep the aspect ratio locked to avoid stretching, or choose “fit” to add padding so the whole picture stays visible. Everything is processed on your device.

faqs.q: Will resizing reduce quality?
faqs.a: Making an image smaller keeps it sharp. Making it larger than the original can look soft, because new detail can’t be created.

faqs.q: What does “keep aspect ratio” mean?
faqs.a: It keeps the width and height in the same proportion, so the image is not stretched or squashed.

faqs.q: What size is best for Instagram?
faqs.a: A 1080 × 1350 portrait (4:5) shows largest in the feed. Square posts are 1080 × 1080.

pitch.title: Want a website that loads fast?

tools.name: JPG to PNG Converter
tools.summary: Convert JPG images to PNG — and PNG or WebP to JPG — in seconds, in your browser. Convert several files at once.
steps: Add your images.
Choose the format to convert to.
Download each file, or all of them as a ZIP.
tools.about: PNG is best for logos, screenshots and graphics because it is lossless and supports transparency. JPG is better for photos because the files are much smaller. Converting a JPG to PNG won’t restore lost detail, but it stops further quality loss when you edit and save again.

faqs.q: Will converting to PNG make my background transparent?
faqs.a: No. A JPG has no transparency to keep, so the background stays as it is. Use a background-removal tool first if you need transparency.

faqs.q: Why is my PNG bigger than the JPG?
faqs.a: PNG stores every pixel without compression loss, so photos become larger. That’s normal.

faqs.q: What happens to transparency when converting to JPG?
faqs.a: JPG can’t store transparency, so transparent areas are filled with white.

tools.name: PDF to JPG Converter
tools.summary: Turn every page of a PDF into a high-quality JPG image. Choose the quality, then download single pages or all pages as a ZIP.
steps: Choose a PDF file.
Pick the image quality — higher quality makes larger images.
Download the pages you need, or all of them as a ZIP.
tools.about: Useful for sharing a page on WhatsApp or social media, adding a document to a presentation, or uploading to forms that only accept images. The PDF is opened and converted inside your browser using the same engine Firefox uses, so private documents stay on your device.

faqs.q: Is there a page limit?
faqs.a: No fixed limit, but very large PDFs take longer and use more memory. On phones, converting at standard quality is faster.

faqs.q: Can it open password-protected PDFs?
faqs.a: Yes — you’ll be asked for the password, which is used only in your browser.

faqs.q: Which quality should I pick?
faqs.a: Standard is fine for screens and WhatsApp. Choose high for printing or for reading small text.

tools.name: Password Generator
tools.summary: Generate strong, random passwords and memorable passphrases using your device’s secure random generator. Nothing is stored or sent.
steps: Choose a length and which characters to include, or switch to passphrase.
Press Generate until you like one.
Copy it straight into your password manager.
tools.about: Strong passwords are long and random. A 16-character password using letters, numbers and symbols would take longer than a lifetime to guess. Passwords here are created with your browser’s cryptographic random generator and are never sent anywhere — and the best way to remember them is a password manager.

faqs.q: Is it safe to generate passwords online?
faqs.a: Here, yes: the password is created on your device and never leaves it. You can even disconnect from the internet and it will still work.

faqs.q: How long should a password be?
faqs.a: At least 12 characters, ideally 16 or more for important accounts like email and banking.

faqs.q: What is a passphrase?
faqs.a: Several random words joined together, like “copper-river-lamp-seven”. They are long, strong and easier to type than random characters.

tools.name: QR Code Generator
tools.summary: Create free QR codes for links, text, WhatsApp chats, Wi-Fi, email and phone numbers. Choose colours and size, then download as PNG or SVG.
steps: Choose what the QR code is for: link, WhatsApp, Wi-Fi and so on.
Fill in the details and pick your colours and size.
Download as PNG for sharing or SVG for printing.
tools.about: QR codes made here are “static”: the information is stored inside the code itself, so they never expire and don’t depend on any website staying online. Put one on business cards, shop counters, menus or flyers. Always test a printed code with your phone camera before printing many copies.

faqs.q: Do these QR codes expire?
faqs.a: No. The content is inside the code, so it works for as long as the link or details inside it are valid.

faqs.q: Which format is best for printing?
faqs.a: SVG. It stays perfectly sharp at any size, from a business card to a banner.

faqs.q: Why won’t my coloured QR code scan?
faqs.a: Scanners need strong contrast. Keep the code dark on a light background, and avoid light colours for the code itself.

tools.name: Random Name Generator
tools.summary: Generate random English names, catchy usernames for social media and gaming, and business or brand name ideas from your own keyword.
steps: Choose English names, usernames or business names.
Set the options — like gender, style or your keyword.
Press Generate, then copy the ones you like.
tools.about: Need a character name for a story, test data for a form, a fresh username or ideas for a new brand? Generate as many as you like. For business names, always check that the domain name and social handles are free and that no one else is already trading under the name.

faqs.q: Are these names real people?
faqs.a: English names combine common first and last names at random, so they are not meant to describe any real person.

faqs.q: Can I use a generated business name?
faqs.a: Yes, they are free to use — but search for the name and check trademark registers before you commit to it.

faqs.q: How can I make a username unique?
faqs.a: Add a word that means something to you, use the number option, or swap one letter. Short and easy to spell is best.

tools.name: Lorem Ipsum Generator
tools.summary: Generate placeholder text by paragraphs, sentences or words — plain or as HTML — for website mockups, designs and templates.
steps: Choose paragraphs, sentences or words, and how many.
Tick “HTML” if you want paragraph tags included.
Copy the text into your design.
tools.about: Lorem ipsum is scrambled Latin that has been used as filler text since the 1500s. It lets you judge a layout without being distracted by real words. Remember to replace it with real content before your website goes live — search engines and visitors both notice placeholder text.

faqs.q: What does lorem ipsum mean?
faqs.a: It comes from a passage by Cicero written in 45 BC, but the words are jumbled so they don’t form readable sentences.

faqs.q: Why not just use real text?
faqs.a: Real text draws attention to its meaning. Placeholder text keeps the focus on fonts, spacing and layout.

faqs.q: Does every paragraph start with “Lorem ipsum”?
faqs.a: Only the first one, if you leave that option ticked. The rest is randomised.

tools.name: YouTube Title Generator
tools.summary: Get click-worthy YouTube title ideas for your topic in different styles — how-to, list, curiosity, beginner and more — with a length check for each.
steps: Type your video topic and, optionally, who it is for.
Pick a style or leave it on “mixed”.
Copy the titles you like and adjust them to your voice.
tools.about: A good title tells viewers exactly what they will get and gives them a reason to click. Keep the most important words near the start, because titles are shortened on phones after about 60–70 characters. Titles are capped at 100 characters on YouTube.

faqs.q: How long should a YouTube title be?
faqs.a: Aim for 50–70 characters so it isn’t cut off, and never more than YouTube’s 100-character limit.

faqs.q: Should I use clickbait?
faqs.a: Make titles exciting, but always deliver what the title promises. Misleading titles lead to viewers leaving early, which hurts your channel.

faqs.q: Should I put keywords in the title?
faqs.a: Yes — include the words people would search for, ideally near the beginning.

tools.name: Instagram Caption Generator
tools.summary: Generate Instagram captions for any topic in the tone you want — fun, professional, inspiring or short — with emojis and a call to action.
steps: Enter what your post is about.
Choose a tone and whether to include emojis and a question.
Copy a caption and make it your own.
tools.about: The first line of a caption is what people see before “more”, so make it count. Ending with a question or a clear call to action invites comments. Instagram captions can be up to 2,200 characters, but short captions often work best for quick, visual posts.

faqs.q: How long should an Instagram caption be?
faqs.a: Short captions suit eye-catching photos; longer captions work for stories, tips and personal posts. The limit is 2,200 characters.

faqs.q: Where should I put hashtags?
faqs.a: At the end of the caption or in the first comment both work. Use our Hashtag Generator to find relevant ones.

faqs.q: Can I use these captions for business posts?
faqs.a: Yes — choose the professional tone and add details about your product or offer.

tools.name: Hashtag Generator
tools.summary: Generate relevant hashtags for Instagram, TikTok, X and LinkedIn from your keywords, then copy them in one click.
steps: Type a few keywords that describe your post.
Choose the platform and how many hashtags you want.
Remove any that don’t fit, then copy the rest.
tools.about: Hashtags help people who don’t follow you find your posts. A mix of broad and specific tags works better than using only the most popular ones, where posts get buried quickly. Instagram allows up to 30 hashtags per post, but 5–15 relevant ones is usually plenty; on LinkedIn and X, 2–5 is better.

faqs.q: How many hashtags should I use?
faqs.a: Around 5–15 on Instagram and TikTok, 2–5 on LinkedIn and X. Relevance matters more than quantity.

faqs.q: Should I use the most popular hashtags?
faqs.a: Mix them. Very popular tags move fast, so smaller, specific tags often bring more of the right people.

faqs.q: Can I use local hashtags?
faqs.a: Yes — add your city, like Lahore or Karachi, to the keywords to get location-based tags.

tools.name: Meta Description Generator
tools.summary: Write SEO meta descriptions that fit Google’s length, include your keyword and invite the click — with a live search result preview.
steps: Enter your page title, main keyword and what makes the page useful.
Pick a description, or edit one in the preview box.
Check the length bar stays green, then copy it into your website.
tools.about: A meta description is the short summary under your page title in Google search results. It doesn’t directly change your ranking, but a clear, relevant description gets more people to click. Google usually shows around 150–160 characters on desktop, so the generator keeps descriptions within that length.

faqs.q: How long should a meta description be?
faqs.a: About 120–160 characters. Shorter can look thin; longer is usually cut off with “…”.

faqs.q: Does Google always use my description?
faqs.a: Not always. Google sometimes picks text from the page that better matches the search, but a good description is used more often.

faqs.q: Should every page have a different description?
faqs.a: Yes. Each page should have its own description that matches what that page is about.

projects.title: Automating multi-store reporting
projects.summary: How I turn the repetitive parts of managing 13 US retail stores into tools and automations — so reports are consistent, ready on time, and I spend my hours on the work that needs a person.
projects.challenge:
I’m the main contact for two US mobile phone dealer organizations that run **13 retail stores** between them. The dealers depend on clear daily, weekly and monthly numbers to see which stores are doing well, where the gaps are, and who needs coaching.

Doing that by hand means repeating the same steps for every store, every day: collecting figures, working out the KPIs, comparing them with targets and turning them into something a dealer can read in a minute. It’s slow, it leaves room for copy-and-paste mistakes, and it has to be ready before the dealers start their day in the US.
projects.approach:
My rule is simple: **if I do the same task more than a few times, I build a tool or an automation for it.**

- **One standard format for every store.** Each store reports the same KPIs — foot traffic, conversion, average ticket, accessory attach rate and sales per staff hour — so stores can be compared fairly.
- **Formulas and automation instead of manual maths.** The KPIs and the gaps against target are calculated automatically, so the numbers are consistent and the same every time.
- **Small web tools for quick checks.** When I need an answer on the spot, a simple tool beats a spreadsheet, so I build small calculators for the checks I repeat most.
- **Built so the team can use it too.** The tools are simple enough for my remote team to run, so the process doesn’t depend on one person.
projects.outcome:
- Reports are **consistent across all 13 stores**, so dealer reviews start from numbers everyone trusts.
- Less time goes into repetitive data work and **more into the parts that need a person**: coaching staff, planning with dealers and fixing what slows a store down.
- The same approach now powers the [free tools](/free-tools) on this website — built for problems I had myself, then opened up for everyone.

**Want the same for your business?** If your team repeats the same task every day, there’s usually a tool that can do it in a minute.

- **Cookies:** small files stored by your browser. See the [Cookie Policy]() for details.

Free tools that run on this site (such as calculators) process what you type in your browser. That data is not sent to or stored on our server.

## How we use your information

- To reply to messages, booking and purchase requests, arrange payment, and deliver tools you buy.

- To send the newsletter you subscribed to. Every email lets you unsubscribe.

- To run, secure and improve the site, and to understand which content is useful.

- To show advertising that helps keep the site and its free tools available.

- To meet legal obligations.

We do not sell your personal information.

## Advertising and Google AdSense

This site may display advertisements served by Google AdSense and other third-party advertising vendors.

- Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this website or other websites.

- Google’s use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visit to this site and/or other sites on the Internet.

- You may opt out of personalized advertising by visiting [Google Ads Settings](https://adssettings.google.com). You can also opt out of some third-party vendors’ use of cookies for personalized advertising at [www.aboutads.info](https://www.aboutads.info/choices/) or, in Europe, [www.youronlinechoices.eu](https://www.youronlinechoices.eu/).

Learn more about [how Google uses information from sites or apps that use its services](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites) and about [how Google uses cookies in advertising](https://policies.google.com/technologies/ads).

Visitors in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland are asked for consent before personalized ads or non-essential cookies are used, through a Google-certified consent tool. You can change your choice at any time using the privacy settings link shown by that tool.

## Analytics

We may use Google Analytics to understand how visitors use the site, such as which pages are viewed and how long visits last. Google Analytics uses cookies and collects information such as your IP address (shortened before storage) and device details. You can opt out using the [Google Analytics opt-out browser add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout).

We may also use Microsoft Clarity to see how visitors use the site through behavioral metrics, heatmaps and session replay, so we can improve the site. Website usage data is captured using first- and third-party cookies and other tracking technologies. For more information about how Microsoft collects and uses your data, see the [Microsoft Privacy Statement](https://www.microsoft.com/privacy/privacystatement).

The free tools remember the last few tools you opened (“Recently used”) in your own browser’s storage. This list never leaves your device, and you can clear it by clearing your browser’s site data.

## Sharing your information

We only share personal information:

- with service providers who help run the site, such as our web host and email provider, only as needed to provide their service;

- with payment providers you choose to pay through, such as a bank, JazzCash, Easypaisa or an international transfer service;

- when required by law, or to protect the rights and safety of the site, its users or others.

## How long we keep information

Contact messages and purchase requests are kept for as long as needed to respond and to keep records of sales, normally up to three years. Newsletter emails are kept until you unsubscribe. Server logs are kept for a limited period for security.

## Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete or receive a copy of your personal information, to object to or restrict how we use it, and to withdraw consent. To make a request, email [usman4588408@gmail.com](mailto:usman4588408@gmail.com). We will respond within 30 days.

California residents may request what personal information we have collected and ask for it to be deleted. We do not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising except through the advertising cookies described above, which you can control as explained.

## Children’s privacy

This site is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has given us personal information, contact us and we will delete it.

## Security

We use reasonable measures to protect your information, including encrypted connections (HTTPS) and restricted access to the admin area. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure.

## Links to other sites

This site links to other websites, such as the Chrome Web Store. We are not responsible for their privacy practices. Please read their policies.
